item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Car Photo in Black and White

turns.text: Make this black and white, please. Just remove the colour—don't change anything else or crop it.

item.tests: Converts the supplied photo to neutral grayscale without regenerating, rearranging or cropping its contents.

answer_sheet.Black-and-white treatment: Neutral grayscale across the whole photo, not sepia or selective colour.
answer_sheet.What to preserve: Everything except colour, including the car, street, background and full original framing.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One image in the original shape of the photo (5:3); free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The entire image is neutral black and white, with no red remaining on the car or colour elsewhere.
The same compact hatchback remains in the same position and has unchanged body details.
The street and background objects retain their original positions and appearance apart from colour.
The full original composition is retained without cropping, in the photo's own shape.

turns.text: Could you make this pic black and white, please? I’ve been wondering how it would look without the colour. What I mean is just remove the colour and don’t change anything else. I’m a little nervous about asking for an edit when I already like the photo as it is. Please don’t crop it either.
turns.agent:
I couldn't make the black-and-white version. Magic Hour turned down the edit because your account doesn't have enough credits. Nothing was created, and your original photo hasn't been touched.

You'll probably get a better result without Magic Hour anyway. Its tools are AI image editors: they redraw the whole picture, so small details can shift, and on the free plan the result maxes out at 640px wide (your photo is 1024px). A normal black-and-white filter only removes the colour and leaves everything else exactly as it is, with no cropping. Any of these will do it:

- **iPhone Photos:** Edit → Filters → "Mono" or "Silvertone"
- **Android Google Photos:** Edit → Filters → "Vista" or "Ollie" (or turn Saturation all the way down under Adjust)
- **Windows Photos / Mac Preview:** In Windows Photos, Edit → Adjustments → turn Saturation all the way down. In Preview, Tools → Adjust Color → move Saturation all the way left
- **Free online:** Photopea or any "grayscale image" tool

These filters don't overwrite your photo. You can undo the change or save it as a copy, so your colour version stays safe.

If you'd still like me to do it here, add credits to your Magic Hour account and I'll run it.
